source_text: παραδοὺς ὁ δεσπότης λέγῃ· «βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος», διὰ τὸ ἰσότιμον καὶ ἰσοσθενὲς καὶ ὁμοούσιον καὶ τὴν εὐκρινίαν τῶν ὑποστάσεων· ὅταν τὸ νῦν περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς λεχθὲν ἑτέρωθι περὶ τοῦ μονογενοῦς ἢ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἀπομέμνηται, διὰ τὰς προλεχθείσας αἰτίας· 36.5 ὅταν τὰ αὐτὰ ἔργα τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνέργειαν ἀμφοτέρας ποιεῖν τὰς ὑποστάσεις διαφόρως διδάσκωσιν, διὰ τὸ ὡς προείρηται· 36.6 ὅταν ἑκάστης ὑποστάσεως δυναμένης δημιουργῆσαι καὶ πάντα ποιῆσαι εὐδόκησεν ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ διὰ μὲν τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ θεοῦ ὑποστῆναι πάντα, διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἁγιασθῆναι, διὰ τὸ ἓν θέλημα τῆς τριάδος καὶ τὸ δείκνυσθαι ἐξ αὐτῆς χορηγεῖσθαι πάντα τὰ καλὰ καὶ διὰ τὸ ἡμᾶς κοινὴν αὐτῇ καὶ ἴσην ἀναπέμπειν εὐχαριστίαν καὶ δοξολογίαν· 36.7 ὅταν τοῖς αὐτοῖς ὀνόμασι κέχρηνται ἐπὶ τῆς μακαρίας τριάδος, οἷον «θεὸς», «κύριος», «ἅγιος», «δίκαιος», «ἀγαθὸς» καὶ ὅσα τοιαῦτα, –πλὴν ὅτι «ὁ πατήρ», μόνος καὶ ἀεὶ πατήρ», καὶ «ὁ ἀληθινὸς υἱὸς καὶ θεός», ἀνάρχως υἱὸς καὶ θεός», καὶ «τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα» ἀνάρχως ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ», –διὰ τὴν τῆς φύσεως καὶ βασιλείας καὶ πάντων κοινωνίαν· τοῦτο δὲ ἐπὶ αὐτῆς μόνης· ὅταν ἐν ἀπορρήτῳ διαλέγωνται, διὰ τὸ ἀεὶ τὸ μυστήριον τῆς πίστεως φυλάττεσθαι μόνοις ἀποκαλυπτόμενον πιστοῖς· ὅταν λέγωσιν τὸν μὲν θεὸν πατέρα γεννήσαντα, τὸν δὲ υἱὸν λόγον γεννηθέντα, τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἐκπορευόμενον, διὰ τὸ θεϊκῶς νοεῖν ἐκ τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἀνάρχως καὶ ἀπαθῶς καὶ μὴ παραπλησίως τῶν κτισμάτων προεληλυθέναι τε καὶ ἡνῶσθαι. 36.8 ὅταν λέγῃ· «ὁ πέμψας με πατὴρ μείζων μού ἐστιν» καὶ ὅσα νενόμισται πρὸς θεότητα εἶναι μικρά, διὰ τὴν δι' ἡμᾶς καὶ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἄρρητον καὶ ἑκούσιον αὐτοῦ οἰκονομίαν. ἐπὶ γὰρ τῆς θεότητος οὔτε τὸ μικρὸν οὔτε τὸ μὴ εἶναι πανταχοῦ χώραν ἔχει. 36.9 ὅταν λέγῃ ὁ υἱὸς ὅτι «ὁ πατήρ μου ἐντολήν μοι δέδωκεν, τί εἴπω καὶ τί λαλήσω, καὶ ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλάλησα», περὶ δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος· «ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ οὐ λαλήσει» καὶ ὅσα τοιαῦτα, διὰ τὴν 41 συμφωνίαν τῶν θείων ὑποστάσεων καὶ διὰ τὸ κοινὰ εἶναι τῆς μακαρίας τριάδος τὰ διδάγματα καὶ χαρίσματα καὶ οὐ διαφωνοῦντα ὡς τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Περὶ τοῦ τὴν ἁγίαν τριάδα ἀκατάληπτον εἶναι. 1.1 Οἱ σπουδάζοντες εἶναι ναὸς κἂν ποσῶς ἄξιος τοῦ οἰκοῦντος ἐν τοῖς πιστοῖς ἁγίου πνεύματος, ὡς ἅπαξ ἔχοντες ἐλλάμπον αὐτοῖς τὸ ἀπρόσιτον φῶς, δοξάζουσιν, ὡς ὁ δεσπότης ἐν τῇ μυσταγωγίᾳ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἐθέσπισεν ἰσοτίμως, τόν τε αὐτογενῆ θεὸν καὶ πατέρα καὶ τὸν ἐξ αὐτοῦ συνυπάρχοντα αὐτῷ ἀγαπητὸν καὶ μονογενῆ υἱὸν λόγον καὶ τὸ μνημονευθὲν ἅγιον πνεῦμα τὸ μόνον ἐκ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ ἀνάρχως καὶ ἀδιαστάτως ἐκπορευθέν· 1.2 τῷ μὲν ὁμοουσίῳ τῆς τριάδος μὴ ἀπιστοῦντες, τρόπον δὲ καὶ διαφορὰν γεννήσεως καὶ ἐκ πορεύσεως οὐ ζητοῦντες· ἐπειδὴ καὶ ταῖς οὐρανίοις λειτουργικαῖς δυνάμεσιν ἄγνωστον, ἄφραστον καὶ φοβερὸν ἐνθυμήσει καθέστηκεν τοῦτο· καὶ τὸ πῶς ἑαυτῇ συνυφέστηκεν ἀνάρχως ἡ ἁγία τριὰς ἔχουσα ἀεὶ ὡσαύτως καὶ κατὰ ταὐτά· καὶ οἷά τε οὖσα ἐπὶ τοῦ αἰωνίου καθημένη θώκου ἐπιβλέπειν ἀβύσσους καὶ σιωπῶσα ἀκούεσθαι καὶ σιωπώντων ἀκούειν· 1.3 καὶ πρὸ τοῦ πρακτέου ἐπίστασθαι τὸ μέλλον· καὶ λόγῳ, καὶ θᾶττον λόγου καὶ μόνῳ τῷ θέλειν πάντα παραγαγεῖν· καὶ πρὶν διαθρήσῃ τις ἐν τῆς καρδίᾳ μόνον δὲ πιστῶς καὶ δικαίως, τὴν ψῆφον εὐθὺς τὴν ἐπὶ τῇ αἰτήσει παρέχειν· καὶ πᾶσι καιρὸν εἰς εὐεργεσίαν ἁρμόζεσθαι· καὶ βραδείαν μὲν εἶναι εἰς ὀργήν, εἰς εὐποιίαν δὲ ἕτοιμον· καὶ χαλεπαίνειν μὲν δι' ἡμετέραν πλημμέλειαν ἀφιέναι δὲ δι' οἰκεῖαν φιλανθρωπίαν τὴν τιμωρίαν· 1.4 ἔτι γε μὴν ἀκατάληπτον αὐτῆς ἐστιν καὶ τὸ πῶς ἓν ἔχει θέλημα, καὶ λαλεῖ καὶ παρέχει κοινὸν ἑαυτῆς· καὶ ἐπισκέπτεται οὐ μᾶλλον εὐεξίαν σωμάτων, ἀλλ' αὐτὴν συντετριμμένην καρδίαν. 1.5 καὶ μὲν δὴ καὶ τοῦτο, πῶς ὑπάρχει ἀόρατος καὶ σεραφικοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς ἀπερίληπτος, λόγῳ καὶ τόπῳ ἀχώρητος, δυνάμει ἀμερής, ἀναφής, ἀμεγέθης, ἀμαθής, ἀπλατής, ἀνείδεος· παντεπίσκοπος, παντεπήκοος καὶ πάντων ἐλπίς· φωτὸς οὐρανίου ὑπὲρ τὸ πολὺ φωτεινοτέρα καὶ παντὸς ὕψους, ὅσον οὐκ ἔστιν εἰπεῖν, ὑψηλοτέρα, καὶ παντὸς νοῦ ἀπείρῳ λόγῳ νοητικωτέρα. 1.6 πῶς γὰρ οὐκ ἔμελλεν τὰ τῆς τριάδος πᾶσιν ἀκατάληπτα τυγχάνειν, ὅτε αὐτὴ πάντων ἐστὶ γενεσιουργὸς καὶ ἀνωτάτω πάσης νοερᾶς, ἔτι μὴν καὶ νοητῆς κτίσεως, μεθ' ἣν ἐπέκεινα παντελῶς οὐδέν, πάντα δὲ
pass_a_gloss: [...] the Master, having handed down, says: 'baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit', it is on account of the equal honour and equal strength and same being and the clear distinctness of the hypostases; whenever the thing now said about God and Father is recorded elsewhere about the only-begotten or the Holy Spirit, it is on account of the causes said before; 36.5 whenever they teach in differing ways that both the hypostases do the same works, the same working, on account of what has been said before; 36.6 whenever, each hypostasis being able to craft and make all things, God and Father was well pleased that through the Son and God all things come to stand, and through the Holy Spirit be made holy, it is on account of the one will of the Trinity and of its being shown that from it all the good things are supplied, and on account of our sending up to it a common and equal thanksgiving and glorifying; 36.7 whenever they have used the same names in the case of the blessed Trinity, such as 'God', 'Lord', 'holy', 'just', 'good' and as many such things (except that 'the Father' is alone and always Father, and 'the true Son and God' is beginninglessly Son and God, and 'the Holy Spirit' is beginninglessly one and the same Spirit of God), it is on account of the sharing of the nature and kingdom and all things; and this in its case alone; whenever they converse in what is not to be spoken, it is on account of the mystery of the faith being always guarded, being uncovered to the faithful alone; whenever they say that God the Father begot, and the Son Word was begotten, and the Holy Spirit proceeds, it is on account of understanding in a godly way that out of the hypostasis of the Father they have come forth, beginninglessly and without suffering and not similarly to the creatures, and have been made one. 36.8 Whenever he says: 'the Father who sent me is greater than me', and as many things as have been thought to be small with respect to deity, it is on account of his unspeakable and willing management on account of us and on behalf of you. For in the case of the deity neither the small nor the not being everywhere has room. 36.9 Whenever the Son says that 'my Father has given me a command, what I should say and what I should speak, and from myself I did not speak', and about the Holy Spirit: 'from himself he will not speak', and as many such things, it is on account of the harmony of the divine hypostases and on account of the teachings and the grace-gifts of the blessed Trinity being common and not disagreeing like those of human beings. [Chapter title:] About the Holy Trinity being ungraspable. 1.1 Those who are eager to be a shrine, even if in some measure worthy, of the Holy Spirit dwelling in the faithful, as having once for all the unapproachable light shining in on them, glorify with equal honour, as the Master laid down by oracle in the initiation of baptism, both the self-born God and Father, and the beloved and only-begotten Son Word who exists together with him from him, and the recalled Holy Spirit, which alone out of his hypostasis has proceeded beginninglessly and without gap; 1.2 not disbelieving the same-being of the Trinity, but not seeking a manner and difference of begetting and outgoing; since even to the heavenly serving powers this has stood unknown, unspeakable and fearful to the thought; and how the Holy Trinity co-subsists with itself beginninglessly, holding always alike and according to the same things; and how it is able, sitting on the eternal seat, to look upon depths, and being silent to be heard and to hear the silent; 1.3 and before the thing to be done to know the coming thing; and by a word, and quicker than a word, and by the willing alone to lead forth all things; and before anyone looks through in the heart, only faithfully and justly, at once to grant the vote upon the request; and to fit for all a season toward well-doing; and to be slow toward anger, but ready toward doing good; and to be harsh because of our fault, but to let go the punishment through its own love of humankind; 1.4 and further indeed ungraspable of it is also how it has one will, and speaks and furnishes in common from itself; and it looks upon not more the good condition of bodies, but the crushed heart itself. 1.5 And indeed also this, how it is unseen and not to be encompassed by seraphic eyes, not to be contained by reason and place, partless in power, untouchable, sizeless, untaught, breadthless, formless; overseer of all, hearer of all, and the hope of all; brighter by far than heavenly light, and loftier than every height, so much as is not possible to say, and more thinking than every mind by an unbounded ratio. 1.6 For how was it not going to happen that the things of the Trinity are ungraspable to all, when it itself is maker of the coming-to-be of all things and uppermost over every thinking, and further indeed thinkable, creation, after which beyond there is wholly nothing, but all things [...]
pass_b_english: … the Master, in handing it down, says, “Baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19), it is because the hypostases are equal in honour, equal in might and consubstantial, and yet clearly distinct. When what is said in one place of God the Father is recorded elsewhere of the Only-begotten or of the Holy Spirit, it is for the reasons given before. When the Scriptures teach in different ways that both hypostases do the same works, the same activity, it is for the reason stated before.

When, though each hypostasis was able to create and make all things, God the Father was pleased that all things should come into being through the Son, who is God, and be sanctified through the Holy Spirit, it is because of the one will of the Trinity, and to show that every good thing is supplied from it, and so that we may send up to it a common and equal thanksgiving and doxology.

When the Scriptures use the same names for the blessed Trinity, such as “God”, “Lord”, “Holy”, “Righteous”, “Good” and the like (except that “the Father” is alone and always Father, “the true Son and God” is Son and God without beginning, and “the Holy Spirit” is, without beginning, one and the same Spirit of God), it is because of their communion in nature and kingdom and all things; and this holds of the Trinity alone. When they speak in veiled terms, it is because the mystery of the faith is always guarded, revealed to the faithful alone. When they say that God the Father begot, that the Son, the Word, was begotten, and that the Holy Spirit proceeds, it is so that we may understand, as befits God, that they came forth from the hypostasis of the Father without beginning and without passion, not as creatures do, and that they are united.

When he says, “The Father who sent me is greater than I” (John 14:28), and whatever else is thought too small for the Godhead, it is because of his ineffable and voluntary economy for our sake and on your behalf. For in the Godhead neither smallness nor not being everywhere has any place.

When the Son says, “My Father has given me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak, and I have not spoken from myself” (John 12:49), and of the Holy Spirit, “He will not speak from himself” (John 16:13), and the like, it is because of the concord of the divine hypostases, and because the teachings and gifts of the blessed Trinity are common, not at odds with one another as those of men are.
That the Holy Trinity is incomprehensible.

Those who strive to be a temple, worthy in some measure, of the Holy Spirit who dwells in the faithful (1 Corinthians 6:19), as men who once for all have the inaccessible light (1 Timothy 6:16) shining within them, glorify with equal honour, as the Master decreed in the mystagogy of baptism, the self-existent God and Father; the beloved and only-begotten Son, the Word, who is from him and coexists with him; and the Holy Spirit just named, who alone proceeded from his hypostasis, without beginning and without interval.

They do not disbelieve the consubstantiality of the Trinity, but neither do they inquire into the manner of begetting and of procession, or the difference between them. For this is unknown even to the ministering powers of heaven, ineffable, and fearful to ponder. So too is how the Holy Trinity co-subsists with itself without beginning, ever the same and in the same way; and how, seated on the eternal throne, it can look upon the depths, be heard while it is silent, and hear those who are silent; and know what is to come before it is done; and bring all things into being by a word, and faster than a word, by willing alone; and, before anyone has searched his own heart (only let it be in faith and righteousness), give at once its verdict on the request; and fit for everyone the right moment for kindness; and be slow to anger but ready to do good; and be provoked by our offences, yet remit the punishment out of its own love for mankind.

More than that, it is incomprehensible how it has one will, and speaks and bestows in common, as one; and how it looks not so much to the good health of bodies as to the contrite heart itself. And this too: how it is invisible and not to be grasped even by the eyes of the seraphim, not to be contained by word or place; without parts in its power, beyond touch, without size, untaught, without breadth, without form; all-surveying, all-hearing, and the hope of all; brighter by far than heavenly light, higher than every height beyond what can be said, and more intelligent than every mind by an infinite measure.

For how could the things of the Trinity fail to be incomprehensible to all, when it is itself the author of all things and highest above every intellectual creation, and indeed every intelligible one? Beyond it there is nothing whatever, but all things …
notes: Khazarzar; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify

choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English turned ὑποστῆναι πάντα (that all things come into being) into 'to sustain all things', reversed the subject of the doxology ('it sends to us thanksgiving'; we send it up to the Trinity), tied 'this holds of it alone' to the wrong clause, gave 'having already preceded and being unified, not as near to creatures' for came forth … not as creatures, and are united, misread τὸ μόνον … ἐκπορευθέν as 'from His only hypostasis' (the Spirit alone proceeded), 'while silencing, hears' for is heard while silent and hears the silent, 'scratches in the heart', 'overshadows' for ἐπισκέπτεται, 'unsearchable … simple, and unyielding' for the string of negative attributes, and 'higher than all noetic' for the intellectual and intelligible creation. A stray '...' after 36.9 cut the section. '(Matt 28:19)' written in full; 1 Corinthians 6:19 and 1 Timothy 6:16 added inline.

choices.english: … the Master, in handing it down, says
choices.why: The section opens mid-clause ('When the mystical teaching …' ends the previous section). Only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.

choices.term: ὅταν … διαφόρως διδάσκωσιν / κέχρηνται / διαλέγωνται / λέγωσιν
choices.english: When the Scriptures teach … use … they speak … they say
choices.why: The subject of the plural verbs is the Scriptures of 36.2; named once more in English for clarity, not added.
Translated as the copy-text reads, beside δι' ἡμᾶς ('for our sake'); see problems.
Printed page number in the copy-text; page debris.

choices.term: Περὶ τοῦ τὴν ἁγίαν τριάδα ἀκατάληπτον εἶναι. 1.1
choices.english: That the Holy Trinity is incomprehensible.
choices.why: Chapter heading where the copy-text's numbering starts again at 1.1 (the opening of the next book); set as its own paragraph.
αὐτογενής here means having being from no other, not 'self-begotten' in a generative sense; the Son and Spirit are the ones 'from him'.
ἀπόρρητος = not to be spoken openly; Didymus links it to the discipline of the mystery kept for the faithful.
The copy-text's article is in the wrong case (τῆς for τῇ); read as 'in the heart'.
Read as it stands (God needs no teacher); possibly a slip for ἀπαθής (impassible), see problems.

choices.english: Beyond it there is nothing whatever
choices.why: The feminine relative is taken of the Trinity, the subject of the sentence; English starts a new sentence so that 'it' cannot be read as creation.

choices.term: πλὴν ὅτι «ὁ πατήρ», μόνος καὶ ἀεὶ πατήρ» …
choices.english: except that “the Father” is alone and always Father …
choices.why: The copy-text's quotation marks in 36.7 are unbalanced; only the names themselves are quoted in English.
